# 2 Baruch Chapter 77 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Baruch's Letters

---

**1** After all these things, when I had written everything down, I, Baruch, went back to the people. They gathered around me in a large crowd.

**2** I told them: "I am going to Babylon. I will plead with the Lord before the captivity begins, so that his wrath does not fall on you."

**3** "I will speak to the Mighty One on your behalf, so you will know he has not forgotten you and that he will show you mercy."

**4** "This is what the Mighty One has said to me: 'I will record in the book of life all the deeds of the righteous, and I will not forget a single work of the righteous.'"

**5** "So go now and let everyone know — those in Babylon and those still in the land — that the days of your captivity will come to an end."

**6** "Do not abandon the covenant of the Mighty One. Do not turn away from the law."

**7** "Remember Zion. Do not forget the festivals and the sacred days. Keep the law of the Holy One and remain holy, as you have been commanded."

**8** "The Mighty One is about to rescue you from your enemies' grasp, because there are righteous people among you who have not abandoned the law."

**9** When the people heard all this, they broke into weeping together, deeply troubled, and cried out loudly.

**10** They said to me: "As the Lord lives, we will do everything you have told us."

**11** Weeping, they sent me away from among them.

**12** I, Baruch, sat down in a field and mourned and fasted for seven days.

**13** After seven days I, Baruch, got up from the ground and took a reed in my hand.

**14** I wrote a letter to the nine and a half tribes in Babylon, tied it around an eagle's neck, and sent it off.

**15** The eagle flew away and reached the nine and a half tribes.

**16** Then I wrote another letter to the two and a half tribes in the land, and to those who were in Jerusalem.

**17** In those days Baruch was found in the city of Babylon.

**18** "Hear, O Israel, the words of Baruch son of Neriah, who has been taken into the captivity of Babylon."

**19** "I am Baruch, the one who was with Jeremiah the prophet. I was shut inside Jerusalem when it was captured."

**20** "Jeremiah commanded me to write these things, and I, Baruch, wrote what he dictated."

**21** "Remember the law of the Holy One. Do not forget the festivals and sacred days. Pray for your captivity to end — it is near."

**22** "Do not give up hope — you will be gathered back from all the nations where you are scattered."

**23** "Stand firm in the law, be zealous in keeping the commandments, and teach them to your children."

**24** "Mourn for Zion; grieve over her. She who was the mother of all of you has been handed over to the nations."

**25** "But grieve for her and do not despair of her, for she will be restored to you. The Mighty One will rebuild her, and he will never permit her destruction again."

**26** "When that time comes, you will go back and live in her. Your enemies will be destroyed, and you will rejoice with great joy."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Prioritizes clarity and natural English flow while preserving the theological and narrative content of the Syriac source.*
